subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Elimination by Aspects
description: Learn Elimination by Aspects in one minute.

hook.text: Choosing a laptop: first eliminate all over $1,000. Then eliminate under 8GB RAM. Two cuts, three options left.

buildup.text: Tversky proposed elimination by aspects: rank your criteria, then cut options that fail each, one by one.

discovery.text: Instead of weighing every feature of every option, you simplify by removing losers sequentially.

twist.text: The order of your criteria changes the winner. Prioritize price first and you get a different laptop.

climax.text: This strategy is fast and practical. But be aware: the order you filter determines the result.

punchline.text: Choice by elimination: fast but order-dependent.

quiz.question: What is the key weakness of elimination by aspects?
options: The order of criteria changes the final choice
It only works with two options

details.summary: Elimination by aspects is a simplifying heuristic where people narrow down choices by sequentially removing options that fail to meet a minimum threshold on the most important attribute first, then the next most important, until one option remains.
details.whyItMatters: When choice sets are large, people cannot evaluate every option on every dimension. Elimination by aspects makes complex decisions manageable but can discard the best overall option if it falls just below a threshold on one attribute while excelling.
takeaways: Options are eliminated by failing to meet a cutoff on sequentially considered attributes
The order of attributes considered determines which option survives
An option that is excellent overall can be eliminated by one slightly below-threshold attribute

faq.question: How does elimination by aspects differ from weighted scoring?
faq.answer: Weighted scoring evaluates every option on all dimensions simultaneously. Elimination by aspects considers one dimension at a time and permanently removes options that fail any single threshold. It is faster but can eliminate the best overall candidate based on one marginal shortfall.

faq.question: When is elimination by aspects a reasonable decision strategy?
faq.answer: When options are numerous and analysis time is limited. When certain minimum requirements are genuinely non-negotiable. When the attributes considered first are clearly the most important. It becomes problematic when attribute ordering is arbitrary or thresholds are too rigid.
